hints.S36_A1: The bus reached the STOP just as the students ARRIVED, so nobody had to WAIT. Ask: which choice means a vehicle came smoothly to a halt at the kerb? 'Departed' means the opposite, and buses do not fly.
hints.S36_A2: The clue is BEFORE LEAVING THE STATION - this journey is ending, not beginning. Ask: which phrasal verb closes a journey on the card reader? 'Erase' would wipe the card, and 'snap' would break it.
hints.S36_A3: It is PEAK HOUR and passengers COULD BARELY MOVE inside the carriage. Ask: is that train full of people or short of them? 'Empty', 'deserted' and 'spacious' all describe the opposite of a crowded carriage.
hints.S36_A4: He is UNSURE WHICH SERVICE TO TAKE while he studies the ROUTE MAP. Ask: does he look sure of himself, amused, or completely unable to work it out? Match the adjective to his confusion, not to his age.
hints.S36_A5: The reason is given: TO ALLOW OTHERS TO BOARD, so the crowd must shift towards the REAR. Ask: which phrase asks passengers to shift back inside a carriage? 'Race' means run, and 'retreat' belongs to an army.
hints.S36_B1: EVERY WEEKDAY signals a habit, so the verb stays present. The subject is one STATION, not the crowds inside it. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S36_B2: BEFORE WE REACHED THE STOP tells you the bus had already gone - finished past time. Ask: what is the past form of this verb? It is irregular, so an -ed ending would be wrong.
hints.S36_B3: THAN is the giveaway: rush hour is measured against MIDDAY - just two rides compared. Ask: for exactly two things, do you need a comparative or a superlative? 'Most' and 'the most' pick a winner out of several.
hints.S36_B4: Bus 65 is ranked against every other bus ON THIS ROUTE - three or more of them. Ask: for a whole group like that, do you need a comparative or a superlative? 'Reliably' is an adverb and cannot follow 'is' here.
hints.S36_B5: SPACE cannot be counted - you never say 'one space, two spaces' about room on a train. Ask: which word partners an uncountable noun? 'Few', 'a few' and 'many' all need things you can count one by one.
hints.S36_B6: JUST tells you neither ride wins - both feel equally smooth. Ask: which pair holds two things EQUAL, and which pairs declare a difference? 'More … than' and 'less … than' would put one line ahead of the other.
hints.S36_B7: The INTERCHANGE did not do anything - it received an action, and BY THE TRANSPORT AUTHORITY names who did it. LAST YEAR fixes it in past time. Ask: which choice is passive and past? Passive = 'be' + past participle.
hints.S36_B8: TOLD COMMUTERS = a reported command, and this one forbids something. Ask: after 'told' + person, which verb form follows - plain, -ing, or an infinitive? And does a negative word sit before that infinitive, or inside it?
hints.S36_C1: The DOORS CLOSED right behind them, so the family moved from the platform to inside the CARRIAGE. Ask: which preposition shows movement entering an enclosed space? 'In' would only tell you where they already are.
hints.S36_C2: Father is heading for the TICKET MACHINE so he can TOP UP his card - he is moving in its direction. Ask: which preposition shows movement in the direction of something, without saying he has arrived yet?
hints.S36_C3: A TUNNEL is enclosed: the train goes in at one end and comes out at the other, EMERGING at the next station. Ask: which preposition takes you inside something and right out the far end? 'Across' needs an open surface.
hints.S36_C4: They HURRIED over an open CONCOURSE to reach the escalator on the FAR SIDE. Ask: which preposition means from one side of an open space to the other? A tunnel word is wrong - nothing encloses them here.
hints.S36_C5: The bus goes by the OLD MARKET WITHOUT STOPPING - it does not enter it and does not circle it. Ask: which preposition means alongside and beyond? 'Around' would send the bus in a loop.
hints.S36_C6: The bus follows ORCHARD ROAD from one end towards the other, STOPPING AT EACH BAY on the way. Ask: which preposition means following the whole length of a road? 'On' would only name the surface it drives upon.
hints.S36_C7: You can LOOK DOWN at the CARS BELOW, so the track is higher and it crosses the EXPRESSWAY. Ask: which preposition means spanning above something? 'Above' is only a position, not a crossing.
hints.S36_C8: The feeder bus LOOPS the ENTIRE ESTATE and comes back to where it started. Ask: which preposition describes a circle or a ring? A straight-line word could never bring the bus back to the same place.
hints.S36_D1: The clue is EVERY DAY, TO SCHOOL AND WORK, BY BUS AND MRT - the same trip again and again. Ask: which box word is the verb for travelling regularly between home and work? A noun cannot follow 'millions of people'.
hints.S36_D2: Passengers TRANSFER BETWEEN DIFFERENT TRAIN LINES WITHOUT LEAVING THE BUILDING. Ask: which box word names a station where lines meet? JURONG EAST and DHOBY GHAUT are the two examples given.
hints.S36_D3: Two clues: it DEPENDS ON THE DISTANCE TRAVELLED, and an amount is DEDUCTED from the card. Ask: which box word names the price paid for one journey? It is a noun - 'the ___ for a journey'.
hints.S36_D4: FEWER CARS are needed, so what shrinks is the jam of traffic on the ROAD. Ask: which box word names too many vehicles clogging the roads? It is a noun, and good bus services cut it down.
hints.S36_D5: They RARELY ARRIVE LATE, and you can plan around the PUBLISHED TIMETABLES. Ask: which box word describes arriving exactly on time? It follows 'known for being', so it must be a describing word.
hints.S36_E1: The underlined word claims the platform BELONGS to somebody, but the class simply WAITED at that place for FIVE MINUTES. Ask: which spelling means 'at that place'? Both sound identical, so choose by meaning.
hints.S36_E2: WALKED is an action verb, and the underlined word tells you HOW he walked - it is not describing a person. Ask: which ending turns a describing word into one that can describe an action?
hints.S36_E3: Find the subject: THE SEATS - more than one. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular past verb, or the plural one? Never match the verb to 'all taken' or to the word standing nearest to it.
hints.S36_E4: MORE is already printed in front of 'crowder', so the -er ending does the same job a second time. Ask: does a long adjective take -er, or a helper word in front of it? Never both at once.
hints.S36_E5: The MRT CARDS belong to all the PASSENGERS - many owners, not one. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only number? And when the owners are many, where exactly does the apostrophe land?
hints.S36_F1: Both sentences describe things YOU do with your CARD - one on boarding, one on leaving. Ask: after 'As well as', does the verb stay plain or take -ing? Then decide which action belongs inside that phrase.
hints.S36_F2: 'Unless' already means IF NOT, so the negative in DO NOT TAP OUT must disappear when you join the two. Ask: which half is the condition, and which is the result? And can 'will' ever follow 'unless'?
